identity.title: Depth Anything 3: Recovering the Visual Space from Any Views

problem.claim: Predict spatially consistent geometry from arbitrary visual inputs, with or without known camera poses.

contributions.claim: DA3 uses a plain transformer backbone and a single depth-ray prediction target, trained with a teacher-student paradigm.
A visual geometry benchmark covering camera pose estimation, any-view geometry, and visual rendering.
DA3 is reported to achieve leading performance across the benchmark and to outperform DA2 on monocular depth estimation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish DA3 through minimal modeling: a nonspecialized transformer backbone and a singular depth-ray target instead of complex multi-task learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report detail and generalization comparable to DA2 under teacher-student training.
On the introduced benchmark, the authors report average gains over VGGT of 35.7% in camera pose accuracy and 23.6% in geometric accuracy across the stated tasks.
The authors report that DA3 outperforms DA2 in monocular depth estimation; all models were trained exclusively on public academic datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper presents DA3 for spatially consistent geometry from arbitrary visual inputs, with optional camera poses.
It argues that minimal modeling is sufficient: a plain transformer and one depth-ray prediction target.
Teacher-student training is reported to produce detail and generalization on par with DA2.
The authors introduce a benchmark spanning pose estimation, any-view geometry, and rendering.
DA3 is reported to surpass VGGT across benchmark tasks and DA2 on monocular depth.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a minimal architecture and singular prediction target to a model evaluated across multiple geometry tasks.

lessons.interpretation: A compact design rationale can make broad evaluation easier to attribute to specific modeling choices.
lessons.application: State the minimal design choices first, then evaluate them on a benchmark whose task coverage matches the claimed scope.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the target genuinely requires task-specific outputs or when broad task coverage is unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, splits, baselines beyond VGGT and DA2, or statistical uncertainty.
The reported average improvements and the DA2 comparison lack per-task conditions and implementation details.
The abstract does not establish that the stated design choices individually caused the reported gains.
